premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes a disordered solid solution in high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperatures.
Specific favorable atomic pair interactions (e.g., Al–Ni) can drive local chemical clustering (short-range order).
This clustering can compromise the single-phase disordered state despite entropy stabilization.
Rapid quenching preserves a random solid solution, while extended annealing promotes clustering.
The competition between entropy-driven disorder and enthalpy-driven clustering governs structural stability.
